claim_text: The special theory of relativity, or simply special relativity, is a scientific theory of the relationship between space and time.
In Albert Einstein's 1905 paper 'On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies', the theory is presented as being based on just two postulates.
The laws of physics are invariant (identical) in all inertial frames of reference, known as the principle of relativity.
The speed of light in vacuum is the same for all observers, regardless of the motion of light source or observer, known as the principle of light constancy.
Relativity is a theorem formulated by Albert Einstein, which states that space and time are relative, and all motion must be relative to a frame of reference.
The natural world allows no 'privileged' frames of reference.
As long as an object is moving in a straight line at a constant speed (that is, with no acceleration), the laws of physics are the same for everyone.

Satellite-based measurement needs to take into account relativistic effects, as each satellite is in motion relative to an Earth-bound user, and is thus in a different frame of reference under the theory of relativity.
